```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`hyperloom` groups four complementary packages. Use `cuvis.r` for Cubert CUVIS
recordings, `tivis.r` for TIVITA recordings, `hyperspectR` for processing and
analysis, and `hyperspectaculR` for spectral visualizations. The metapackage
installs these members and offers a small inventory API.

## Install and inspect

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("CTTIR/hyperloom", dependencies = NA)
```

The member packages are required dependencies. Their optional modelling
backends and the vendor SDK are configured separately according to the member
documentation. The metapackage does not download instruments, SDKs, or datasets
when loaded.

```{r inventory}
hyperloom::hyperloom_packages()
hyperloom::hyperloom_status()
```

`hyperloom_status()` reports installed versions in library search order. Save
the report alongside `sessionInfo()` and the project dependency lockfile to
record which software was available. A version report does not establish that
an instrument backend or scientific method has been validated.

## Work with explicit namespaces

The following synthetic example exercises `hyperspectR` without clinical data,
files from an instrument, or a vendor SDK:

```{r synthetic-cube}
cube <- hyperspectR::hs_example_cube()
hyperspectR::hs_plot_rgb(cube)
```

Use the reading functions documented in `tivis.r` and `cuvis.r` for real
recordings. Inspect wavelength, geometry, calibration, and acquisition metadata
before passing data between packages. The suite installation does not replace
those checks or promise arbitrary object compatibility.

`hyperspectaculR` provides its own visualization interfaces and synthetic
examples:

```{r visualisation}
visual_cube <- hyperspectaculR::hsa_demo_cube()
hyperspectaculR::hsa_fusion(visual_cube)
```

These examples show software usage rather than validated physiological or
clinical inference.

## Attach all members when useful

```{r attach, eval=FALSE}
library(hyperloom)
```

Attaching `hyperloom` attaches all four members using R's ordinary `Depends`
mechanism. Member startup hooks and messages still apply. Using
`hyperloom::hyperloom_status()` instead reads installation metadata without
attaching the suite or initializing the CUVIS SDK. Explicit namespaces make
scripts easier to read when multiple packages export similarly named functions.

## Instrument setup and licenses

`cuvis.r` can install without the Cubert SDK in stub mode. Reading and processing
vendor recordings requires the SDK and a correctly configured installation;
consult [cuvis.r](https://github.com/CTTIR/cuvis.r). TIVITA file reading is handled
by [tivis.r](https://github.com/CTTIR/tivis.r).

`hyperloom` is MIT licensed. Each member package and vendor component keeps its
own license and installation requirements.
